content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: no-cost break shift, IVR callbacks and one late cross-skill move, predicted 94.5% service level for 15:00-20:00 at no extra cost.","why":"A sick wave (12 absences on payments vs a usual 2.6, 13 on general vs 2.4) has cut staffing, pushing service level down to 56.8% on payments and 72.4% on general at 13:30. For the 15:00-20:00 window, even doing nothing is predicted to reach 93.7%, above the 80% target. P1 nudges that to 94.5% (payments 93.8%, general 95.4%) and cuts predicted abandons from 1.6% to 1.3%, at zero cost and with no policy issues. It does this by delaying payments breaks by 30 min, offering IVR callback on payments 15:00-16:00 and 18:00-19:30 and on general 18:00-19:00, and moving 1 cross-skilled agent from general to payments 19:00-20:00. No escalation is needed.","trade_offs":["P2 reaches 95.9% with 1.1% abandons but costs INR 858. It cancels payments coaching and pushes 20% of some enquiries to chat, which affects customers.","P3 reaches 95.4% with 1.1% abandons for INR 720 of evening overtime on 3 payments agents.","P1 relies on callbacks, so some customers wait for a call back rather than being answered live.","P1 moves 1 agent off general 19:00-20:00, but general is still predicted at 95.4%, the same as with no action.","P0 (no action) already meets the target at 93.7%, so P1 is a low-risk improvement rather than a rescue."],"watch":"Check payments service level and the callback backlog around 15:30 and again at 18:00. Further fever absences could widen the gap beyond these predictions; if payments heads toward 80%, consider P3's overtime."}
